options: This is the library where knowledge is free for all.

options: The poem was wrote by Tagore.

questions.rule: Passive = was/were + past participle. The past participle of write is written.

questions.rule: A positive sentence with should takes a negative tag: shouldn't it?

questions.prompt: Make a sentence that shows a wish.
questions.rule: For a wish about the present, use the past form: I wish ... were.

chat: The poem is a prayer, isn't it?
options: Yes, it does. Tagore pray for a free India.
Yes, it are. Tagore praying for a free India.
Yes, it is. Tagore prays for a free India.
questions.rule: Answer an is question with it is; Tagore (he) takes prays.

options: It was written by Rabindranath Tagore.
questions.rule: Singular it takes was, and the passive needs the past participle written.

questions.source: What a beautiful prayer this is!
options: This a very beautiful prayer is.
This is a very beautiful prayer.
This is very a beautiful prayer.
questions.rule: What a ...! becomes a statement with very: This is a very beautiful prayer.

options: I wish I know the answer now.

I wish I will know the answer now.
questions.rule: A wish about the present uses the simple past: I wish I knew.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: Let's sing the national anthem, will we?
Let's sing the national anthem, shall we?
Let's sing the national anthem, don't we?
questions.rule: A sentence beginning with Let's always takes the tag shall we?

chat: Do you want to visit Santiniketan?
options: Yes! I wish I could go there.
Yes! I wish I can go there.
Yes! I wishing I could go there.
questions.rule: After I wish, use the past form: could, not can.

questions.source: Tagore translated the poem into English.
options: The poem translated by Tagore into English.
The poem is translated into English by Tagore.
The poem was translated into English by Tagore.
questions.rule: Simple past active becomes was + past participle: was translated.

options: If I were the principal, I will make the library free for all.

If I were the principal, I would make the library free for all.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Present perfect passive = has been + past participle: has not been broken.

questions.after: parents work in the city, live with their grandmother.
questions.rule: whose shows possession: the children whose parents (= their parents).
Nobody is negative, so the tag is positive, and it uses they: were they?
Passive: object first, then was + past participle: was awarded.

chat: Who will speak first on 'India of my dreams'?
options: I am speaking first, aren't I?
I am speaking first, am not I?
I am speaking first, isn't it?
questions.rule: The tag for I am is aren't I?

chat: Which city did Tagore come from?
options: He came from Kolkata, which he was born in 1861.
He came from Kolkata, who he was born in 1861.
He came from Kolkata, where he was born in 1861.
questions.rule: For a place followed by a full clause (he was born there), use where.
Keep the tense (worked) and use very. hard is the adverb here; hardly means almost not.

questions.source: I am sorry that I cannot speak Bengali.
options: I wish I could speak Bengali.
I wish I can speak Bengali.
I wish I cannot speak Bengali.
questions.rule: Regret about the present: I wish + past form. cannot becomes could.

Knowledge must be shared with everyone.

questions.rule: A suggestion with Let's ends with the tag shall we?

chat: I watched the Republic Day parade on TV.
options: What a grand parade it were!
What a grand parade it was!
How a grand parade it was!
questions.rule: Use What a + adjective + noun; singular it takes was.

options: By whom was this beautiful prayer written?
By whom this beautiful prayer was written?
By whom was this beautiful prayer wrote?
questions.rule: Who becomes By whom; keep question order: was + subject + past participle.

questions.source: It is a very noble dream.
options: How a noble dream it is!
What a noble dream it is!
questions.rule: With a singular noun, use What a + adjective + noun; drop very.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Yesterday: discussed. Every student: was asked. A place + full clause: where.

options: I wish I had listened to my teacher yesterday.
I wish I listened to my teacher yesterday.
I wish I have listened to my teacher yesterday.

questions.before: The poet longed for a nation in
questions.rule: After a preposition (in), use which. Never write in where or in that.
Passive question: Wh-word + was + subject + past participle.

chat: Nobody has forgotten the speech for tomorrow, I hope.
options: No, ma'am. Everyone has prepared it, hasn't it?
No, ma'am. Everyone have prepared it, haven't they?
No, ma'am. Everyone has prepared it, haven't they?
questions.rule: Everyone takes a singular verb (has) but the tag uses they: haven't they?

chat: Why didn't you come to the book fair?
options: I was ill. If I was well, I would have gone.
I was ill. If I had been well, I would go.
I was ill. If I had been well, I would have gone.
questions.rule: Imagined past: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle.

questions.source: The child was too afraid to raise his head.
options: The child was so afraid that he could not raise his head.
The child was so afraid that he can not raise his head.
The child was very afraid that he could raise his head.
questions.rule: too ... to becomes so ... that + negative; past tense needs could not.

options: Let the views of others are respected.
Let the views of others be respect.
Let the views of others be respected.
questions.rule: An order in the passive: Let + object + be + past participle.
